title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description: About unPLUG Dining unPLUG Dining is an AI-powered digital growth platform that helps restaurant brands grow first-party revenue, increase guest lifetime value, and unify guest data across channels. As a vendor-agnostic orchestration layer, we connect ordering, loyalty, marketing, and analytics into one decision-ready system, turning digital ordering into personalized guest experiences across web, mobile, and in-store. We build and run first-party apps, loyalty programs, payment integrations, marketing tools, and a Customer Data Platform for enterprise restaurant brands in the US. About the role Forward Deployed Engineer · Istanbul, Türkiye · Full-time, Hybrid · Development We're hiring our first dedicated Forward Deployed Engineer. You'll be the engineer our restaurant brand partners work with every week: you take their integrations, launches, production issues, and requests from first message to resolved in production. Until now, every engineer at unPLUG carried this work on top of product development. As our brand portfolio grows, the last mile needs a dedicated owner. You'll act like a technical lead for each brand you support, and you'll turn what you learn in the field into tooling and product so the next brand launches faster. This is a hands-on engineering role, not a pre-sales or account management role. You write and ship production code every week. What you'll do Integrations Build, configure, and maintain integrations with POS, ordering, payments, loyalty, and marketing partners (APIs, webhooks, data syncs) Own integration health: monitoring, alerting, reconciliation, and fixing data mismatches before a brand notices them Deployments Lead brand launches and rollouts end to end: configuration, environment setup, app builds and store releases, data migrations, go-live checklists, and post-launch hypercare Coordinate across Mobile, Web, Platform, Dashboard, and Design so every launch runs as one plan with one owner Customer support Own the FDE triage queue: reproduce, debug, and resolve production issues across apps, payments, loyalty, and data pipelines within SLA Find root causes using Sentry, CloudWatch, ClickHouse, and logs, then fix the issue yourself or route it with a clear write-up Build AI-assisted support workflows that triage, answer, and resolve common issues automatically Client requests Be the technical point of contact in weekly calls with brand IT and Marketing teams Turn requests into clear scopes: what's needed, how big it is, and whether it's a configuration change, a one-off, or a product feature Ship small requests yourself and hand larger ones to product teams with a crisp brief Make the next brand easier Turn repeated work into tooling, templates, runbooks, and self-serve admin features Bring what you see in the field back into the roadmap What we're looking for Strong engineering fundamentals and hands-on experience shipping and supporting production systems that real customers depend on Integration experience: REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, idempotency, retries, and mapping data between systems that don't agree Strong production debugging: you read logs and traces, write SQL, and work from symptom to root cause without a runbook Backend depth in Python, plus enough React or Flutter to work across the stack when an issue crosses layers Clear communication with non-technical stakeholders: you explain trade-offs simply, write crisp updates, and can say "not yet" with an alternative Ownership through resolution: you stay calm under pressure and close the loop with the customer Product-minded engineering: you can tell a one-off request from a pattern, and you push patterns into the product AI-native workflow: you use AI to move faster while keeping independent judgment, quality, and correctness Fluent written and spoken English; our brand partners are in the US Note on seniority: We care less about years on paper and more about ambition, ownership, and talent. AI has changed the baseline; strong engineers adapt quickly, validate rigorously, and ship impactful work. Nice to have Restaurant tech experience: POS, online ordering, or loyalty platforms (for example Toast, Square, Olo, Thanx, Punchh) Payments integrations and reconciliation Mobile release operations: App Store Connect, Google Play, Firebase, Apple and Google Wallet passes AWS (Lambda, SQS, Fargate) and Terraform Prior experience as an FDE, solutions engineer, support engineer, or in professional services Building LLM-powered tools or agents for support or operations Bonus: Opus lover 😄 Tech stack: Python (Flask, FastAPI), Go, React, Flutter, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis, AWS (Lambda, Fargate, SQS, CloudWatch), Terraform, Sentry, Firebase, CI/CD What success looks like First 30 days: You know our product surface and integrations, own the triage queue for your first brands, resolve production issues end to end, and join weekly customer calls. By 90 days: You've led at least one brand launch or major integration from kickoff to go-live, you run customer calls for your brands, issues are resolved within SLA, and at least one runbook or automation has removed repeated manual work. By 180 days: Brands see you as their technical owner, repeated requests have become self-serve or product features, and product engineers spend noticeably less time on interrupt-driven support. How we work High trust, high ownership: you own your brands and are accountable for their reliability in production Fast iteration cycles with direct customer feedback AI-native by default: execution is faster, judgment matters more Why unPLUG Real ownership: end-to-end responsibility for the brands and integrations you support Visible impact: your work reaches real guests and enterprise restaurant partners the same week you ship it Serious engineering problems: POS, payments, loyalty, marketing, and data integrations under real constraints Shape the role: you're our first dedicated FDE, so you'll define how this function works High-trust team: low bureaucracy, fast shipping, high standards Location and schedule Istanbul, hybrid: 3 to 4 days a week in person Our brand partners are in the US, so this role needs regular overlap with US business hours (Istanbul afternoons and some evenings) on a predictable support schedule

title: Senior Software Engineer (Backend)
description: About AppNation We build AI-powered mobile apps that reach millions of users worldwide. Since 2021, AppNation has been creating products across AI, productivity, and mobile experiences. Our apps, including Genie, Translate AI, and Arch, have reached 90M+ users globally and ranked among the top apps in 30+ countries. We are a team of builders, designers, and engineers who move fast, take ownership, and create products used by millions. About the Role We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Backend) to design, build, and evolve the backend systems behind our AI-powered mobile apps. You’ll work on production systems that power mobile experiences used by millions of users, building reliable APIs, data-intensive services, asynchronous workflows, and integrations with AI and third-party platforms. This is a hands-on engineering role with strong ownership across system design, implementation, testing, performance, and production reliability. You’ll also help raise the engineering bar through technical decisions, code reviews, mentoring, and better development practices. What You’ll Do Design, build, and maintain scalable backend services and APIs using Node.js and TypeScript. Own backend features from technical design and implementation through testing, deployment, observability, and production validation. Design reliable distributed and asynchronous workflows using message brokers, queues, background workers, and event-driven patterns. Build AI-powered product capabilities and integrate backend systems with LLMs, AI providers, and internal AI platforms. Design and optimize relational data models using PostgreSQL and MySQL, including indexing, query optimization, migrations, transactions, and concurrency considerations. Use Redis effectively for caching, distributed coordination, rate limiting, queues, and other appropriate workloads. Design systems with failure in mind, applying appropriate timeout, retry, idempotency, fallback, backpressure, and graceful-degradation strategies. Write comprehensive unit and integration tests and contribute to end-to-end testing of critical product flows. Investigate production issues using logs, metrics, traces, and profiling; identify root causes and implement lasting improvements. Contribute to architectural decisions, technical design reviews, code reviews, and engineering standards. Work effectively with Docker and containerized environments and understand how backend services operate on Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure. Collaborate closely with mobile, AI, product, and infrastructure teams to turn product requirements into reliable technical solutions. Use modern AI-assisted development tools effectively for coding, testing, debugging, research, and engineering productivity without compromising correctness or code quality. Mentor other engineers and help improve engineering practices across the team. What We’re Looking For 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong hands-on ownership of production backend systems. Strong production experience with Node.js and TypeScript. Strong understanding of backend fundamentals, including HTTP, REST APIs, authentication, authorization, concurrency, networking, and application security. Strong experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL and MySQL, including schema design, indexing, query execution and optimization, transactions, locking, migrations, and data integrity. Strong experience with Redis and a solid understanding of caching strategies, invalidation, and appropriate in-memory data patterns. Hands-on experience designing distributed systems and reasoning about scalability, reliability, consistency, concurrency, and failure modes. Production experience with asynchronous and event-driven systems using Kafka, RabbitMQ, Pub/Sub, or similar technologies. Strong understanding of patterns such as idempotency, retries, timeouts, eventual consistency, message delivery semantics, and failure recovery. Strong testing discipline, including unit and integration testing, mocking, testable design, and automated quality checks. Hands-on experience with Docker and familiarity with Kubernetes concepts and containerized production environments. Working knowledge of Google Cloud Platform and fundamental cloud concepts such as compute, networking, IAM, managed databases, storage, and observability. Experience debugging and improving production systems using metrics, logs, traces, and other observability signals. Familiarity with CI/CD workflows and modern software delivery practices. Experience building AI-powered backend capabilities and integrating applications with LLMs, AI APIs, or AI platforms. Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools as part of the daily engineering workflow while independently validating architecture, correctness, security, and maintainability. Strong ownership, technical judgment, communication skills, and the ability to make pragmatic engineering decisions in a fast-moving product environment. Why AppNation? Build and scale products reaching millions of users globally. Work with talented people in a fast-moving AI-first environment. Take ownership and see your impact directly in the products you build. Grow quickly with opportunities to lead projects and shape technical decisions. Enjoy competitive compensation and benefits, including private health insurance, meal and commute support, relocation support, and flexible working options. Our Hiring Process Application Review → Interview → Technical Assessment → Final Interviews At AppNation, we set ambitious goals and challenge ourselves to build products that reach millions of people. We value curiosity, ownership, and continuous growth. If this role excites you and you're ready to make an impact, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now, we're excited to meet you!

title: Software Engineer in Test— Embedded Systems
description: We are looking for a Software Engineer in Test to build the automated testing that decides whether a Q12 build is ready to fly. This is a hands-on, technical role focused on test automation: writing the regression suites that run on every change, keeping the simulation and bench infrastructure that runs them healthy, and turning problems seen in real flights into tests that catch them next time. You will join a quality function that is being built out rather than maintained. Today one engineer covers end-to-end system testing; you will be the automation half of that team, working alongside them and reporting to our SQA Lead. There is a lot of ground with no coverage yet, which means real scope to decide how testing works here rather than inheriting someone else's framework. About SiFly Aviation At SiFly, we’re building a new category of aircraft: vertical-takeoff, long-endurance drones that deliver helicopter-level performance at drone economics. After thousands of flight tests and years of engineering, our NDAA-compliant platform flies more than 2 hours in hover or 3 hours in forward flight on a single charge — matching the capability of traditional helicopters at a fraction of their cost and operational burden. We merge aerial robotics, perception, and onboard intelligence to cut complexity and minimize human intervention, and our unique approach to communications and networking unlocks remote operations from day one. It’s an ambitious mission, and we’re a small team that moves fast. The role You will spend most of your time writing tests and the infrastructure they run on: automated regression across flight software, autonomy, MAVLink interfaces, camera and video pipelines, connectivity and failover, over-the-air updates, and the operator-facing apps. You will own the bench and simulation setups in Ankara, keep them faithful enough to real aircraft that a green result means something, and triage the failures that come out of them — including the system-level factory test code that validates a finished aircraft on the production line. You will work closely with the SQA Lead in Santa Clara, the QA engineer already covering end-to-end testing, and the flight-software, embedded platform, autonomy, and applications teams whose changes you gate — close enough to development that quality is part of everyday work rather than a step at the end. What you’ll do Build the automated regression suites. Design and write automated tests covering flight software, autonomy features, MAVLink interfaces, camera and video pipelines (H.264/HEVC, WHIP/WHEP), the detect-and-avoid stack, telemetry, and operator workflows — and keep them fast and trustworthy enough to run on every change. Run simulation and bench scenarios. Build and maintain SITL and HITL scenario tests for takeoff and landing, mission execution, failsafes, detect-and-avoid, GPS degradation, sensor noise, comms delays, and the long tail of edge cases — and flag where simulation stops matching the aircraft. Keep the test infrastructure running. Wire tests into CI so they trigger automatically, run nightly and batch validation jobs, and deploy simulator and test instances locally and on remote servers so any engineer can run a meaningful test without booking aircraft time. Own the bench in Ankara. Set up and maintain the hardware test rigs, keep them representative of current aircraft configuration, and make them available to the rest of engineering rather than a resource only you can use. Test the full connected system. Multi-link connectivity and failover across 5G, Wi-Fi 6, and Wi-Fi HaLow; over-the-air update and rollback via Mender; cloud and backend integration over MQTT and REST; and the Pilot, Crew, HQ, and mobile apps against the embedded platform. Turn field problems into regression tests. Capture and organize logs, MAVLink and telemetry, video, and perception output from real flights, reproduce the failure, and land it in the automated suite so it stays fixed. Own the system-level factory test code. Work with manufacturing on the functional test scripts that validate a built aircraft on the production line, so factory test has a real owner inside quality engineering. Triage and route failures. Do first-pass triage on failing runs, produce failure artifacts and logs that make the cause obvious, and route each issue to the right owner quickly instead of adding it to a list. Test by hand where automation cannot reach. Run exploratory and end-to-end testing on real aircraft and pre-release checks, and write clear, reproducible reports on what you find. Required experience Minimum 3+ years of professional experience writing software — as a software engineer who moved into testing, or as a test engineer who writes production-quality code. This is an engineering role: you will spend your days writing and reviewing code, not executing test scripts. A bachelor’s degree or higher in a related program — Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or similar. Strong Python. For test automation, log analysis, orchestration, and tooling — you write test code the way you would write product code, and expect it to be reviewed. Test design. You can take a feature and work out what actually needs testing: boundary and edge cases, failure modes, and pass/fail criteria that hold up — then write it down as a test plan and a reproducible bug report. Linux and system-level debugging. Comfortable owning quality across a distributed system: debugging across processes, containers, networks, and the hardware/software boundary on Linux. CI and version control. Practical experience wiring tests into CI — GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, or similar — and working day to day in Git with code review. Hardware proximity. Some exposure to embedded, robotic, or hardware-in-the-loop testing, or enough curiosity and aptitude to get there quickly — this role is on the bench as much as at a desk. Expected to be heavy user of AI and to be aware of AI development workflows. Advanced English language skills and strong written and verbal communication — able to coordinate clearly with the SQA Lead and the wider team in Santa Clara. Based in or able to relocate to Ankara — this is an on-site role with regular hands-on aircraft and bench work. Nice to have MAVLink, ROS, PX4, or comparable autopilot and robotics stacks · SITL, HITL, or hardware-in-the-loop testing of embedded systems · Gazebo, Isaac Sim, AirSim, or game-engine-based simulators · RTSP, GStreamer, or WebRTC video testing and camera simulation · the pytest ecosystem, or comparable frameworks used seriously · Docker and cloud-based CI/CD · OTA testing with Mender, and Yocto or embedded Linux · network emulation and connectivity failure injection · manufacturing or production functional test experience · flight-log analysis and telemetry tooling · QA dashboards, log viewers, or failure-triage tooling · familiarity with UAV regulatory context such as Remote ID and ADS-B · a valid SHGM (Turkish DGCA) remote-pilot licence for the Q12’s İHA weight class — İHA1 (4–25 kg) or İHA2 (25–150 kg) — ideally with beyond-visual-line-of-sight authorization. What success looks like Automated regression runs on every change, and a green result is trusted well enough that nobody quietly re-tests by hand afterwards. Any engineer can spin up a representative test locally or on the bench in minutes, without booking an aircraft. Bugs found in the field land in the regression suite within days, not quarters, and stay fixed. Connectivity failover, OTA update and rollback, video workflows, and operator actions are exercised safely and repeatably before any real flight. Factory functional test has a real owner, and production can validate a built aircraft without pulling engineers off development. Failures arrive at the right owner with the logs and artifacts already attached — and the SQA Lead can rely on your results without re-verifying them. Details Job type: Remote contract-based employment. Location: On-site position in Istanbul, Turkey — working closely with our Santa Clara team.
